subject: Re: Deployment mode & EU/APAC data residency — next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Nilsson <sofia.nilsson@nordbank.se>; Johan Eriksson <johan.eriksson@nordbank.se>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-28T08:15:00+01:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — deployment mode + residency

Hi Sofia / Johan,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on requirements and risks for production: 

Summary of requirements you confirmed:
- Production must keep customer PII and transaction logs within the EU (primary).
- APAC support needed for a small subset of users, but any APAC traffic must not cause EU production data to be copied out of the EU.
- Prefer private networking (VPC) and customer-managed KMS for keys; legal will want SOC 2 evidence + DPA.
- Latency SLO: 100–150ms p95 for core inference calls in EU zones.

Options we discussed (high level):
1) Hosted API (EU region): fastest to go live; supports regional data residency + KMS; cross-region routing is by policy (we can restrict reads/writes to EU) but fallback to other regions would need your sign-off.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput, still hosted in your cloud region(s), stronger isolation, can be provisioned in EU only.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed control plane option, recommended for regulated production.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll send the SOC2 overview and our RFP response (attached).
- Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up with your infrastructure/legal folks to confirm DPA/KMS expectations and whether a Private deployment is required for go-live?
- If Private is required, we’ll share a rough project timeline and checklist (network, HSM/KMS, audit logs, OOB cadence).

I’ve attached the draft RFP answers and SOC2 summary. If helpful, we can spin up a sandbox in the EU region this week for a short performance validation.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: Nordbank_RFP.pdf, Redwood_SOC2_OVERVIEW.pdf

From: Sofia Nilsson <sofia.nilsson@nordbank.se>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Johan Eriksson <johan.eriksson@nordbank.se>
Date: 2027-02-28T09:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — deployment mode + residency

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from infra/legal: 

- For production, Legal is strongly leaning toward Private (VPC or on-prem) so that we can enforce that EU data never leaves EU boundaries. Hosted EU is acceptable only if we get contractual assurances and a clear proof that cross-region routing is disabled by default.
- APAC users: they'd prefer a read-only edge in APAC for latency, but any edge must not store or replicate EU customer data. Can Redwood support an APAC edge that proxies requests to EU origin without caching PII?
- We will need the SOC2 Type II report and a DPA signed before procurement can proceed. Also please include your third-party subprocessor list.

Could you include Marissa and Neha in the follow-up call — they’ll own the technical assessment and procurement respectively. Proposed times: tomorrow 10:00–10:30 CET or Tuesday 14:00 CET.

Best,
Sofia
Head of Cloud Architecture | Nordbank
sofia.nilsson@nordbank.se

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-02-28T12:30:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — deployment mode + residency

Hi Sofia — great, thanks for the clarifications. Quick answers and proposal: 

APAC edge / cross-region routing
- Yes, we can support an APAC edge that proxies requests to an EU origin without persisting PII in APAC. We call this a regional proxy mode; it enforces no-local-persistence and strips any KV/cache that contains PII. We’ll document exactly what’s sanitized.

Hosted EU vs Dedicated vs Private
- Hosted EU: fastest (days) and can be constrained to EU regions with KMS integration, but requires contract language limiting cross-region failover. Good for PoC and smaller workloads.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity in EU-only pools; recommended if you want predictable latency under load and stronger isolation without full private deployment overhead. Provisioning lead time: ~3–4 weeks after contract.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): recommended for regulated production and full control. Typical delivery timeline: 8–12 weeks depending on network and KMS integration details. We’ll provide a checklist (network CIDR, peering, firewall rules, KMS/HSM endpoints, audit access).

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick sync (30m) tomorrow 10:00 CET — confirm with Marissa/Neha and Johan.
2) I’ll drop the SOC2 Type II report, subprocessor list, and a short doc that maps residency controls to the RFP items.
3) If Private is required, we’ll schedule a technical scoping call with our Solutions engineer and your network team to produce a timeline.

Sandbox: I can provision an EU sandbox with no production data within 24 hours for performance checks (no PII). Link: https://app.redwood.ai/sandbox/nordbank

Are you ok with the proposed timeslot?

Thanks,
Aditya

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_OVERVIEW.pdf (attached again)

From: Sofia Nilsson <sofia.nilsson@nordbank.se>

We’ll take the sandbox perf validation next week and confirm whether Private is required for go-live after our legal review. For the follow-up call, 10:00 CET tomorrow works — I’ve booked it.

Sofia
